heuristic.applicability: Prefer after blue appears held/co-moving with the closed gripper and the main risk is transport into or placement within an open drawer whose destination differs from training. It can execute the whole cut and overlap, but source acquisition outside the demonstrated source range is better handled by the blue-frame prior. destination_field must be blue_goal.

handoff.entry_conditions: drawer_position is strictly above 0.26 m and blue is outside or held; red is on/being released over the pad; destination_field resolves to the current calibrated blue_goal. Prefer entry after blue/TCP co-motion with closed fingers when using this prior specifically for insertion.
handoff.exit_conditions: Unchanged simultaneous task success: drawer open, red fully on pad at valid z, and blue fully inside the drawer cavity at valid z in one observation. Release and high TCP retreat remain observed continuation, not extra evaluator conditions.
handoff.failure_signatures: Goal is inconsistent with an open drawer; IK fails or reaches joint limits; blue does not follow the closed TCP; TCP/blue approaches lip or wall; drawer falls to 0.26 m or below; red containment is lost; or final blue center/rotated extent/z is outside the evaluator bounds.
handoff.overlap_role: All [600,stop) actions remain supervised, including the complete [600,850) predecessor overlap. Thus this model can receive control before blue grasp despite being specialized for destination anchoring.
handoff.successor_readiness: No learned successor. Continue through demonstrated release and retreat when needed, then defer to framework success evaluation. If blue is still outside and source displacement is the dominant issue, continue with the blue-frame prior instead.

heuristic.limitations: A translated goal can be unreachable and the point goal does not encode drawer wall/lip geometry or a collision-free route. World-aligned orientation is not invariant to a rotated drawer, for which no orientation argument or demonstrated variation exists. Pickup of a far-displaced blue block is only conditioned, not invariant. A closed gripper and co-motion are observable cues, not proof of grasp. No wall-impact, drawer-closing or insertion-recovery behavior is demonstrated.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: At each replan, build_inputs resolves and freezes the causal blue_goal position in chunk_context. encode_targets subtracts that same point from every commanded TCP position, retaining world 6-D orientation and native gripper scalar. decode_action adds the current chunk destination, projects 6-D orientation to SO(3), calls shared IK from measured joints and reports diagnostics. The standard DiffusionBackbone remains unchanged. No augmentation is used because arbitrary destination shifts could violate workspace and drawer geometry.
heuristic.rationale: In demo1000 the held blue is transported from about (-0.401,0.290,0.280) at 870 toward the drawer, is near the drawer above it by 930, is lowered from z about 0.272 at 950 to about 0.082 at 970, and is released inside by 990 before retreat. Demo1001 shows the same destination relation with shifted timing. The blue_goal x value is calibrated from drawer position and final blue centers cluster near that goal. The expected benefit is exact target translation with a changed drawer opening/goal during approach and insertion, reducing reliance on memorized world coordinates. Robot state, source offset, red containment residual and absolute destination position retain feasibility and simultaneous-task dependencies.
heuristic.statement: Drawer-destination anchored Cartesian targets for confined placement. Learn TCP target position relative to the causal blue_goal point in a world-aligned destination frame, world 6-D orientation and gripper scalar. This makes the final approach, lowering, release and retreat translate exactly with the observed drawer goal rather than with the carried block.

assignment.subgoal: Primary responsibility: finish the predecessor red release/retreat context, acquire the blue block outside the drawer, lift and transport it to the open drawer cavity, lower it inside, release it, and retreat to a high clear pose. The intended object is blue; the red block visible at segment entry is only the predecessor object still being lowered/released. Observed contact/motion: at observation 600 red is still pinched near the pad at z about 0.032-0.037 m; by 700 red is settled at z about 0.020 m and the open gripper is retreating toward blue; around 800 the TCP descends over blue; by 850 blue is pinched and lifted; later it is carried to the drawer, lowered to z about 0.063 m, released, and the TCP retreats to z about 0.323 m. Final observations in all occurrences simultaneously show drawer_position about 0.297, red near (-0.176 to -0.177,-0.298 to -0.304,0.020), and blue near (-0.171 to -0.173,0.073 to 0.074,0.063), satisfying the supplied one-observation completion rule. The demo1000 final front image supports blue in the drawer, red on the outside pad, and the open drawer. Purpose/expected benefit: retaining the long release-to-pick overlap should make this independently trained insertion model usable from intermediate transition states; demonstrated success does not establish recovery from dropped blue blocks, drawer collisions, or unseen placements.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: Compare decoded FK TCP position, rotation angle and gripper scalar to each demonstrated commanded TCP target. Destination subtraction/addition and 6-D label conversion preserve commanded poses; nonunique IK joints are allowed.

contract.cut_relation: Every action in all twelve assigned [600,stop) segments is supervised, retaining the full [600,850) red_transfer overlap before the destination-specialized insertion portion.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is [TCP position offset from causal chunk blue_goal in metres (3), world rotation 6-D (6), gripper scalar (1)]. The destination frame is world aligned and translated to the observed blue_goal. Slot 0 represents t-1 and execution uses slots 1..8 for t..t+7. decode_action adds the frozen destination, Gram-Schmidt projects rotation to SO(3) with a finite degeneracy fallback, and invokes panda_kinematics.solve_ik from freshly measured joints.
contract.parameter_semantics: destination_field selects the calibrated observed blue_goal point in world metres. It is resolved from the causal current observation at every replan and frozen only for that execution chunk; it is not an arbitrary coordinate or actuator input.
